findings.title: Identity Propagation and Delegation
findings.description: The system supports machine identity via OAuth2 client credentials with client_id attribution. However, it does not support on-behalf-of flows — there is no mechanism to distinguish between an agent acting under its own service identity vs. acting on behalf of a specific human user.
findings.gap: No identity propagation (JWT token exchange, on-behalf-of flow, X-User-Id headers). A payments service processing charges on behalf of users cannot attribute actions to the originating user through the authorization chain.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2 token exchange or on-behalf-of flow via Cognito, adding a user identity claim to the token that the authorizer extracts alongside client_id. Log both actor (agent) and subject (user) in audit records.

compensating_controls: Require calling services to include user context in request metadata while implementing proper token exchange
Limit agent to read-only scope (payments:read) until identity propagation is implemented

findings.title: Concurrency Controls
findings.description: The idempotency mechanism in _idempotent_put performs a get_item followed by a put_item without a DynamoDB ConditionExpression. Two concurrent requests with the same idempotency key could both pass the existence check and both write, creating a TOCTOU race condition.
findings.gap: No DynamoDB conditional writes (ConditionExpression attribute_not_exists(pk)) on the idempotency record. The append-only design prevents data corruption for charge/refund items (each has a unique pk), but the idempotency guarantee has a narrow race window under concurrent agent instances.
findings.recommendation: Add a DynamoDB conditional put with attribute_not_exists(pk) on the idempotency record write. Catch ConditionalCheckFailedException and retry the read to return the existing result.

compensating_controls: Add ConditionExpression attribute_not_exists(pk) to idempotency record put_item
Limit concurrent agent instances to 1 per client_id during pilot

findings.title: Rate Limiting and Throttling
findings.description: No explicit rate limiting configuration in the SAM template. API Gateway applies default account-level throttling (10,000 req/s burst) but no per-client usage plan or per-method throttling is defined.
findings.gap: Default API Gateway limits are too generous to protect against a runaway agent loop. No per-client throttling exists.
findings.recommendation: Define an AWS::ApiGateway::UsagePlan with per-client rate limits in infra/template.yaml. Associate Usage Plans with API keys mapped to OAuth client_ids.

compensating_controls: Add API Gateway Usage Plans with per-API-key throttling
Deploy WAF with rate-based rules in front of API Gateway

findings.title: Blast Radius and Transaction Limits
findings.description: No configurable transaction limits exist. An agent can issue unlimited charges or refunds at machine speed. The only protection is API Gateway's default throttling (traffic rate), which does not cap business-domain impact.
findings.gap: No maximum charges per hour, no maximum refund amount per session, no spend caps per agent identity.
findings.recommendation: Add configurable per-client transaction limits (max_refunds_per_hour, max_charge_amount_per_session) enforced at the handler level before writing to the ledger.

compensating_controls: Implement per-client_id hourly charge/refund counters in DynamoDB
Set CloudWatch alarm on refund volume anomalies

findings.title: Draft/Pending State
findings.description: The Charge schema defines a status enum including 'pending', but the code sets status to 'succeeded' immediately in create_charge. All write operations are committed upon execution with no reviewable intermediate state.
findings.gap: No draft/pending workflow exists. An agent creating a charge or refund commits it immediately — there is no mechanism for human review before finalization.
findings.recommendation: Implement a two-step charge flow: create_charge initially writes with status='pending', then a separate confirm_charge endpoint transitions to 'succeeded'. The schema already supports the 'pending' status value.

compensating_controls: Implement an orchestration-layer approval gate before calling the payments API
Limit agent to read-only scope until pending workflow is implemented

findings.title: Configurable Approval Gates
findings.description: No configurable approval gates exist. All operations with valid authentication and authorization execute immediately. No operation-level flags to require human approval.
findings.gap: No mechanism to configure specific operations (e.g., refunds above a threshold) to require human approval before execution.
findings.recommendation: Add configurable approval thresholds for high-value operations. Operations exceeding thresholds write with status='pending_approval' and await a separate approve/reject endpoint call.

compensating_controls: Deploy an orchestration layer (Step Functions) with human approval tasks for high-value operations
Implement amount-based routing at the agent orchestration level

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: Error responses include a structured Error schema with code, message, and correlation_id fields. HTTP status codes are semantically appropriate (409, 422, 404). However, no explicit retryable boolean or retry category is included.
findings.gap: No retryable indicator in error responses. Agents must infer retryability from HTTP status codes alone.
findings.recommendation: Add a retryable boolean field to the Error schema. Map: 409→false, 422→false, 404→false, 5xx→true, 429→true.

compensating_controls: Agent can infer retryability from HTTP status codes
Document retry semantics per error code in OpenAPI spec

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: Tests run offline against DynamoDB Local stub. CI pipeline provides automated testing. RUNBOOK references --config-env prod implying environment separation. No explicit staging environment IaC in the repository.
findings.gap: No staging environment definition in the repository. Agents cannot be tested against a production-equivalent environment from this codebase alone.
findings.recommendation: Add a samconfig.toml with staging environment configuration and document staging deployment procedure.

compensating_controls: Use SAM local for agent testing against DynamoDB Local
Deploy SAM stack to separate AWS account as staging

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: OpenAPI spec versioned (1.4.0), URL path versioning (/v1/), CI validation. No breaking change detection in pipeline.
findings.gap: No automated breaking change detection in CI. An API change removing a field would pass CI without alerting consumers.
findings.recommendation: Add an OpenAPI diff step to GitHub Actions workflow (e.g., oasdiff breaking) that fails on backwards-incompatible changes.

compensating_controls: Manual review of OpenAPI spec changes in PRs
Behavioral tests catch implementation regressions

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: RUNBOOK.md documents CloudWatch alarms (payments-5xx >1%, payments-idempotency-conflict >10/min, payments-ddb-throttle). These alarms are not defined in the SAM template.
findings.gap: Alerting configuration not codified in infrastructure-as-code. Alarms may drift or fail to be replicated in new environments.
findings.recommendation: Add AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm resources to infra/template.yaml for the three documented alarms.

compensating_controls: Alarms likely exist in production (documented in RUNBOOK)
Manual verification against RUNBOOK during deployment

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: Agent-facing surface fully defined as IaC (SAM template). GitHub Actions CI implies PR-based review. No drift detection configured.
findings.gap: No infrastructure drift detection. Manual changes to deployed stack would not be detected.
findings.recommendation: Add AWS Config rules or scheduled CloudFormation drift detection.

compensating_controls: SAM deployments overwrite drift on each deploy
Manual drift detection via CLI

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: CI pipeline includes OpenAPI spec validation, linting, type-checking, and pytest. Behavioral contract tests prove idempotency. No breaking change detection or consumer-driven contract testing.
findings.gap: No automated detection of API-breaking changes before production.
findings.recommendation: Add OpenAPI breaking-change detection step to CI pipeline. Consider Pact for consumer-driven contracts.

compensating_controls: OpenAPI spec validation catches malformed specs
Behavioral tests catch implementation regressions

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: Three behavioral tests cover idempotent retry, conflict detection, and scope enforcement. Limited test breadth — no coverage of validation errors, not-found, refund flow, or edge cases.
findings.gap: No tests for validation error responses (422), not-found (404), refund flow, or boundary conditions.
findings.recommendation: Add test cases for validation errors, GET not-found, refund_charge flow, and missing Idempotency-Key rejection.

compensating_controls: OpenAPI spec with strict schema validation provides runtime validation
Type checking (mypy strict) catches type-level errors

findings.title: Event Emission for State Changes
findings.description: The system uses an append-only DynamoDB ledger but does not emit events for state changes. No SNS, EventBridge, SQS, or webhook integration exists.
findings.gap: State changes only observable via polling GET /charges/{id}.
findings.recommendation: Consider adding DynamoDB Streams with EventBridge integration to emit charge.created and refund.created events.

findings.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
findings.description: No rate limit headers (X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After) returned in API responses. No rate limit documentation in OpenAPI spec.
findings.gap: Agents cannot self-throttle based on approaching rate limits.
findings.recommendation: Add X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Limit response headers. Document throttle limits in OpenAPI spec.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Classification
findings.description: Financial data with proper scoping. Tokenized sources, no raw PAN. API responses exclude sensitive fields. OAuth scopes differentiate access. Only B3 (formal classification metadata) is absent.
findings.gap: No formal data classification metadata (sensitivity tags, field-level annotations).
findings.recommendation: Add classification tags to DynamoDB table in IaC (DataClassification: Financial-Internal).

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to INFO: B1 clear (API responses properly scoped, tokenized data), B2 clear (OAuth scopes differentiate access), only B3 absent (no formal classification metadata).
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: DATA-Q1 evaluates at B3 INFO because agent-facing APIs properly exclude sensitive fields (tokenized payment source, scoped responses) and access differentiation exists via OAuth scopes. No formal classification metadata is the only gap.

b1.reasoning: API responses return only id, amount, currency, status, created_at. Payment source is tokenized — raw PAN never accepted. Sensitive fields properly excluded.

b2.reasoning: OAuth scopes payments:read vs payments:write differentiate access levels. GET endpoint requires only read scope.

b3.reasoning: No DynamoDB table tags with classification labels, no field-level sensitivity annotations, no PII detection tooling.

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: No data quality scores, completeness metrics, or data profiling for ledger data.
findings.gap: No formal data quality monitoring for the payments ledger.
findings.recommendation: Consider adding operational metrics for ledger completeness.

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: No data catalog or metadata layer describes the ledger data semantically. OpenAPI spec documents API contract but no dedicated catalog exists.
findings.gap: No machine-discoverable data catalog for stored data.
findings.recommendation: Register data model in AWS Glue Data Catalog with semantic descriptions.

evaluations.title: Documented API Interface
evaluations.reason: REST API fully documented via OpenAPI 3.1.0 spec with three endpoints, validated in CI.

evaluations.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
evaluations.reason: OpenAPI 3.1.0 spec at openapi/payments.yaml, contract-first, validated in CI.

evaluations.title: Idempotent Write Operations
evaluations.reason: All write endpoints require Idempotency-Key header. Implementation stores keys with hash verification. Contract tests prove the guarantee.

evaluations.title: Structured Response Format
evaluations.reason: All responses are application/json with well-defined schemas and explicit Content-Type headers.

evaluations.title: Asynchronous Operation Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — Lambda timeout is 15s, no long-running workflows detected.

evaluations.title: Machine Identity Authentication
evaluations.reason: OAuth2 client credentials via Cognito with client_id attribution in Lambda authorizer.

evaluations.title: Scoped Permissions (Least Privilege)
evaluations.reason: OAuth scopes (payments:read/write) and per-function IAM policies scoped to specific DynamoDB actions.

evaluations.title: Action-Level Authorization
evaluations.reason: Action-level authorization via OAuth scopes enforced at handler level (_require_scope). Tests verify enforcement.

evaluations.title: Credential Management
evaluations.reason: No hardcoded credentials. Cognito pool via parameter, table name via env var, runtime JWKS validation.

evaluations.title: Immutable Audit Logging
evaluations.reason: Authenticated principal (client_id) logged for every write via structured JSON logging. CloudWatch Logs are append-only. X-Ray tracing active.

evaluations.title: Agent Identity Suspension
evaluations.reason: Cognito app client can be disabled immediately, denying all subsequent token validations.

evaluations.title: Compensation and Rollback
evaluations.reason: Append-only ledger with refunds as first-class compensating operations. Nothing hard-deleted. Reversible by design.

evaluations.title: Queryable Current State
evaluations.reason: GET /charges/{chargeId} exposes current charge state for agent inspection before action.

evaluations.title: Circuit Breakers and Resilience
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — service only calls DynamoDB (AWS infrastructure with SDK-managed retry), no external service-to-service dependencies.

evaluations.title: Graceful Degradation Signaling
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no P0 priority designation or critical path assignment.

evaluations.title: Data Residency and Sovereignty
evaluations.reason: Tokenized payment data without PII. No raw PAN stored. Single-region deployment. No evidence of applicable residency constraints for tokenized financial metadata.

evaluations.title: Selective Query Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — only single-resource GET endpoint exists, no list/query endpoints with unbounded results.

evaluations.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
evaluations.reason: Strict OpenAPI schema validation (additionalProperties: false, required fields, patterns, min/max) enforced at API Gateway. Structured 422 error response.

evaluations.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
evaluations.reason: created_at (ISO-8601 UTC) on all entities. Append-only design ensures data is always authoritative. DynamoDB strong consistency.

evaluations.title: PII Redaction in Logs
evaluations.reason: Logs contain only operational data (correlation_id, client_id, charge_id). No PII logged. Code explicitly states no secrets are logged.

evaluations.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
evaluations.reason: All field names are human-readable and semantically meaningful (amount, currency, status, created_at). No legacy abbreviations.

evaluations.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
evaluations.reason: X-Ray active, structured JSON logging via Powertools, X-Correlation-Id propagated and logged.

evaluations.title: Business Outcome Metrics
evaluations.reason: ChargeCreated metric published via aws_lambda_powertools Metrics (namespace Payments).

evaluations.title: Rollback Capability
evaluations.reason: SAM deployment with immutable versioned artifacts. Rollback via redeploying previous artifact. Documented in RUNBOOK.

evaluations.title: Encryption at Rest for Agent-Accessible Data
evaluations.reason: DynamoDB SSESpecification SSEEnabled: true. Point-in-time recovery enabled.

items.summary: Address critical safety controls: concurrency race condition, rate limiting, and human-in-the-loop mechanisms for write operations.
Implement identity propagation, transaction limits, error response improvements, staging environment, and engineering governance hardening.
Expand test coverage, add event emission, rate limit headers, data classification metadata, and catalog registration.

recommended_actions.action: Fix idempotency race condition with DynamoDB conditional writes
recommended_actions.rationale: Narrow TOCTOU window in idempotency mechanism could allow duplicate charges under concurrent agent load. Single code change resolves.

recommended_actions.action: Deploy per-client API Gateway Usage Plans and throttling
recommended_actions.rationale: Protects against runaway agent loops at machine speed. Enables self-throttling via rate limit headers.

recommended_actions.action: Implement pending/approval workflow for high-value operations
recommended_actions.rationale: Enables human oversight for agent-initiated payments above configurable thresholds. Schema already supports pending status.

recommended_actions.action: Add business transaction limits per agent identity
recommended_actions.rationale: Caps blast radius of agent errors independently of traffic-rate throttling.

recommended_actions.action: Add OpenAPI breaking change detection to CI
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents silent API contract breakage that would cause agent tool failures.

recommended_actions.action: Codify CloudWatch alarms in SAM template
recommended_actions.rationale: Ensures alerting is reproducible and version-controlled alongside the service.
